source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  classical
  induction p using MvPolynomial.induction_on with
  | C r =>
      have h : (algebraMap (MvPolynomial ℕ ℂ) CascadeField) (MvPolynomial.C r)
          = algebraMap ℂ CascadeField r := by
        rw [← MvPolynomial.algebraMap_eq, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
      rw [h, Derivation.map_algebraMap, MvPolynomial.pderiv_C, map_zero]
  | add p q hp hq => simp only [map_add, hp, hq]
  | mul_X p i hp =>
      have hXi : (algebraMap (MvPolynomial ℕ ℂ) CascadeField) (MvPolynomial.X i) = fx i := rfl
      have hL : (pderiv k) (p * MvPolynomial.X i)
          = p * (pderiv k) (MvPolynomial.X i) + MvPolynomial.X i * (pderiv k) p := by
        rw [Derivation.leibniz]
        simp only [smul_eq_mul]
      rw [map_mul, hXi, Derivation.leibniz, hp, hL, map_add, map_mul, map_mul, hXi]
      simp only [smul_eq_mul]
      by_cases hik : i = k
      · subst hik
        rw [fpderiv_fx_self, MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_self, map_one]
      · rw [fpderiv_fx_of_ne hik, MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_of_ne hik, map_zero]

theorem weightScaleAlgEquiv_pderiv {lam : C} (h : lam ≠ 0) (j : ℕ) (a : JetPoly C Unit) :
    MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) (weightScaleAlgEquiv h a)

theorem weightScaleAlgEquiv_pderiv {lam : C} (h : lam ≠ 0) (j : ℕ) (a : JetPoly C Unit) :
    MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) (weightScaleAlgEquiv h a)
      = MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ j) * weightScaleAlgEquiv h (MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) a)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  induction a using MvPolynomial.induction_on with
  | C c =>
      have h2 : weightScaleAlgEquiv h (MvPolynomial.C c : JetPoly C Unit) = MvPolynomial.C c :=
        weightScaleAlgHom_C lam c
      rw [h2, MvPolynomial.pderiv_C]
      simp
  | add p q hp hq =>
      rw [map_add, map_add, map_add, map_add, hp, hq]
      ring
  | mul_X p n hp =>
      have hX : weightScaleAlgEquiv h (MvPolynomial.X n : JetPoly C Unit)
          = MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * MvPolynomial.X n := weightScaleAlgEquiv_X h n
      set d : JetPoly C Unit :=
        MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) (MvPolynomial.X n : JetPoly C Unit) with hddef
      have hdw : weightScaleAlgEquiv h d = d := by
        by_cases hn : ((), j) = n
        · rw [hddef, ← hn, MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_self, map_one]
        · rw [hddef, MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_of_ne (Ne.symm hn), map_zero]
      have hkey : MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * d = MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ j) * d := by
        by_cases hn : ((), j) = n
        · rw [← hn]
        · rw [hddef, MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_of_ne (Ne.symm hn), mul_zero, mul_zero]
      have hleibL := (MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) :
        Derivation C (JetPoly C Unit) (JetPoly C Unit)).leibniz
          (weightScaleAlgEquiv h p) (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * MvPolynomial.X n)
      have hleibC := (MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) :
        Derivation C (JetPoly C Unit) (JetPoly C Unit)).leibniz
          (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) : JetPoly C Unit) (MvPolynomial.X n)
      have hleibR := (MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) :
        Derivation C (JetPoly C Unit) (JetPoly C Unit)).leibniz p (MvPolynomial.X n)
      simp only [smul_eq_mul, MvPolynomial.pderiv_C] at hleibL hleibC hleibR
      have hRHSexp : weightScaleAlgEquiv h
            (MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) (p * MvPolynomial.X n))
          = weightScaleAlgEquiv h (MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) p)
              * (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * MvPolynomial.X n)
            + weightScaleAlgEquiv h p * d := by
        rw [hleibR, map_add, map_mul, map_mul, hX, hdw]
        ring
      have hLHSexp : MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) (weightScaleAlgEquiv h (p * MvPolynomial.X n))
          = MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ j) * weightScaleAlgEquiv h (MvPolynomial.pderiv ((), j) p)
              * (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * MvPolynomial.X n)
            + weightScaleAlgEquiv h p * (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * d) := by
        rw [map_mul, hX, hleibL, hleibC, hp]
        ring
      rw [hLHSexp, hRHSexp]
      linear_combination (weightScaleAlgEquiv h p) * hkey

    weightScaleAlgEquiv h (weightPolyDeriv a)
      = MvPolynomial.C lam * weightPolyDeriv (weightScaleAlgEquiv h a)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  induction a using MvPolynomial.induction_on with
  | C c =>
      have h1 : weightPolyDeriv (MvPolynomial.C c : JetPoly C Unit) = 0 :=
        Derivation.map_algebraMap _ c
      have h2 : weightScaleAlgEquiv h (MvPolynomial.C c : JetPoly C Unit) = MvPolynomial.C c :=
        weightScaleAlgHom_C lam c
      rw [h1, h2, map_zero, h1, mul_zero]
  | add p q hp hq =>
      rw [map_add, map_add, map_add, map_add, hp, hq]
      ring
  | mul_X p n hp =>
      have hleib := weightPolyDeriv.leibniz p (MvPolynomial.X n)
      simp only [smul_eq_mul] at hleib
      have hCd : weightPolyDeriv (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * MvPolynomial.X n
          : JetPoly C Unit)
          = MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * MvPolynomial.X (n.1, n.2 + 1) := by
        have hl := weightPolyDeriv.leibniz
          (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) : JetPoly C Unit) (MvPolynomial.X n)
        simp only [smul_eq_mul] at hl
        have hC0 : weightPolyDeriv (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) : JetPoly C Unit) = 0 := by
          simp [weightPolyDeriv]
        rw [hl, weightPolyDeriv_X, hC0, mul_zero, add_zero]
      have hleib2 := weightPolyDeriv.leibniz (weightScaleAlgEquiv h p)
        (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * MvPolynomial.X n)
      simp only [smul_eq_mul] at hleib2
      have hpow : (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ (n.2 + 1)) : JetPoly C Unit)
          = MvPolynomial.C lam * MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) := by
        rw [← map_mul, pow_succ]
        ring_nf
      have hLHS : weightScaleAlgEquiv h (weightPolyDeriv (p * MvPolynomial.X n))
          = weightScaleAlgEquiv h p
              * (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ (n.2 + 1)) * MvPolynomial.X (n.1, n.2 + 1))
            + MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * MvPolynomial.X n
              * (MvPolynomial.C lam * weightPolyDeriv (weightScaleAlgEquiv h p)) := by
        rw [hleib, weightPolyDeriv_X, map_add, map_mul, map_mul, weightScaleAlgEquiv_X,
          weightScaleAlgEquiv_X, hp]
      have hRHS : MvPolynomial.C lam
            * weightPolyDeriv (weightScaleAlgEquiv h (p * MvPolynomial.X n))
          = MvPolynomial.C lam * (weightScaleAlgEquiv h p
              * (MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * MvPolynomial.X (n.1, n.2 + 1))
            + MvPolynomial.C (lam ^ n.2) * MvPolynomial.X n
              * weightPolyDeriv (weightScaleAlgEquiv h p)) := by
        rw [map_mul, weightScaleAlgEquiv_X, hleib2, hCd]
      rw [hLHS, hRHS, hpow]
      ring

### The multiplier avoids its own coordinate — one Bell reduction

`HTGeometry/ProductLawJetReduction.lean` (axiom-clean) supplies the step the terminal-scaled Bell
reduction needs, and the cancellation that makes it work.

The jet `δX_k` has multiplier `logSum_k + (v_k'/v_k)(X_k)·δX_k`, and the second term looks like it
involves the `k`-th coordinate.  It does not: `δX_k = (∏_(j<k)Q_j)·v_k(X_k)`, so the terminal factor

`(v_k'/v_k)(X_k)·δX_k = v_k'(X_k)·∏_(j<k)Q_j(X_j)`  (`totalLog_eq_of_ne_zero`),

and when `v_k` is linear this is a constant times the head product (`totalLog_linear`), free of `X_k`.

`(1/X_k)·∏_(i≤k)X_i = ∏_(i<k)X_i` — and it is why the tower's logarithmic law stayed polynomial.

**Why `(9)` costs nothing beyond a Lipschitz derivative.**  The primitive inside `P` cancels one copy
of the profile, and the transport commutes with differentiation because its kernel does not see the
evaluation point.  The domination for differentiating under the integral sign is the kernel's *first
moment*: a Lipschitz derivative makes the differentiated second difference `O(s)` uniformly in the
base point, and `s·k(s)` is integrable on the whole positive ray — at the origin because the factor
`s` cancels the pole, at infinity because the kernel decays.  No second-derivative bound enters.

**`(14)` is pure algebra.**  With `W = χF` the product rule gives `W′ = χ′F + χF′`, additivity splits
the transport, and `([R,χ]F)′ = [R,χ′]F + [R,χ]F′` — itself the product rule plus `R∘d/dL = d/dL∘R` —
removes the derivative of `F` from inside the commutator.  Substituting `(9)` gives the display.

**The three walls that put `(14)`'s right side in the block class.**  `χG′` is supported on a
terminal ray and decays at rate `δ`, so its block norm is a geometric series whenever `σ < δ`; a
one-sided source has only finitely many nonzero negative blocks, which is why the two-sided rate-one

corpus's `gammaWallCommutator`, whose two-sided `O(e^{-|L|})` wall is already proved.  The
